topic: App retention before and after a new onboarding flow
decision: whether to keep the new onboarding flow launched on 1 June or go back to the old one

columns.cohort_size: users who signed up that month
columns.retained_users: users still active on that day
columns.retention_pct: retained_users as a percentage of cohort_size
columns.paid_conversion_30d_pct: percentage of the cohort who bought a subscription within 30 days
columns.avg_lessons_first_30d: average lessons completed per user in the first 30 days

findings.text: The January cohort is the largest (18,400 sign-ups), the New Year rush.
Day-30 retention rose from an average of 22.3% for the January to May cohorts (old onboarding) to 31.4% for June to August (new onboarding).
Day-1 retention is about 70% for every cohort, before and after the change.
Lessons completed in the first 30 days rose 12% with the new onboarding.
Only about 13% of early-2026 users are still active after 90 days.

A TV campaign ran from June to August, the same months as the new onboarding, so part of the gain may come from different kinds of users. The September cohort, after the campaign, still reached 28.6% at day 30.
Paid conversion within 30 days rose from 3.1% to 3.9% over the same cohorts.
Data runs to 2 November 2026, so the September cohort is only measured to day 30 and August to day 60.
A user counts as retained on day N if they completed a lesson on day N or later.

main.gist: The new onboarding raised day-30 retention (and paid conversion)

caveat.gist: A TV campaign ran at the same time as the new onboarding

facts.q: What was day-30 retention for cohorts with the old onboarding and with the new onboarding, in percent?
What was the 30-day paid conversion rate before and after the new onboarding, in percent?
